name: Covid-19 genome sequence classification benchmark
description: The rapid spread of the COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in an unprecedented amount of sequence data of the SARS-CoV-2 genome -- millions of sequences and counting. This amount of data, while being orders of magnitude beyond the capacity of traditional approaches to understanding the diversity, dynamics, and evolution of viruses is nonetheless a rich resource for machine learning (ML) approaches as alternatives for extracting such important information from these data. It is of hence utmost importance to design a framework for testing and benchmarking the robustness of these ML models. This paper makes the first effort (to our knowledge) to benchmark the robustness of ML models by simulating biological sequences with errors. In this paper, we introduce several ways to perturb SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences to mimic the error profiles of common sequencing platforms such as Illumina and PacBio. reputation: A niche benchmark from the bioinformatics ML literature, mainly used to study robustness under synthetic sequencing errors rather than broad leaderboard competition.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; performance depends heavily on the chosen perturbation/error model and may not reflect real-world sequencing noise perfectly.
